title: Zeno Speed
subtitle: The earth mocks the masses, bestowing dust and death as presents.

items.text: Zeno Speed

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: They wanted to send rookies into the war zone to get some hands-on experience. I signed up and proved myself better than most, so they let me go.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I was part of the third group.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: When? Saturday, probably. I don't remember. Anyway, it was around noon when we got off the plane.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The sun, the sizzling sand, and a bunch of rookies. Ah, Juhalerat sure knew how to give us a warm welcome.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Before we took off, some of the recruits saw black coffins being unloaded off a plane. They started to panic.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: When they found out that the coffins held the remains of the previous group of rookies, even more chickened out.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: In the end, I was the only one who flew to Juhalerat, carrying the experimental equipment that the others were supposed to handle.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I guess the instructor wanted to use me to test their new toys out in the field.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Those fist-sized boom bombs, packed with volatile Efreetine, could turn a giant boulder into a pile of confetti.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: It was probably because I can fly that they dared to trust me with those things.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And then there was this tiny radar, modified from the Type 76 experimental bug, which picked up preset channels. It was Zeno's latest masterpiece.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I was excited at first, thinking I was gonna do something big there.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Maybe snag a few shiny medals to show off to the wimps back at the academy.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You know, because only the toughest soldiers deserve to be sent to the front lines.
City, Juhalerat

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Juhalerat was a dump of a city. I got off the plane and then onto a truck.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I thought it'd be all dirt and grime, like the mud caked on their truck tires.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Turned out, there were more trees than I'd thought.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The mountains outside the city shone with a pale white glow, like shrapnel glinting in the sun.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: "The mighty Hindu Kush, where even eagles dare not fly." So exclaimed the instructor before we left.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I still remember the silence in the truck, everyone keeping their mouths shut. I figured it was 'cause of the dust on the road.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Soon enough, the truck stopped, the driver cursing and honking at us to get off.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And then there we stood, like a bunch of imbeciles, dazed and confused under the scorching sun of Juhalerat.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Seriously? Is no one coming to pick us up? Did they just throw us off the truck and leave us here?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hello? Comrade? Shouldn't someone be coming to take us to the base?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hey, comrade. Do you know the way? Here, the way to here.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I chatted with a few people and showed them the map in my pocket, but nobody seemed to care.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: They looked at me as if I were a rabbit, but when's the last time you saw a rabbit with the talons of a hawk?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Well, I guess our local comrades must've been busy. How could they spare someone to pick us up when they were at war?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Or maybe they just forgot about us. Anyway, I kept waiting and waiting, for the longest, longest time ...

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: For ten freaking minutes! When the blistering sun finally got to me, I decided I wasn't going to stand around like an idiot any longer!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Alright, guess this is where we part ways, comrades. Good luck! Всего хорошего!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I had a letter and a map in my pocket, though all soaked from my leaky bottle. But that was okay, they were still readable.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I followed the map aimlessly around the city, feeling like I was going in circles.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Until a kind local recognized my uniform and stopped me in the street.

items.speaker: Kind Local
items.text: You are from Zeno, yes? Welcome, friend!

items.speaker: Kind Local
items.text: Are you going to the base? It's not far ahead. Just go straight for 120 steps, turn into the alley with the red wall, and continue for another 210 steps.

items.speaker: Kind Local
items.text: Then turn right and come to an intersection with two sacred figs. Turn right again and you will find Farouk's tea shop. Go down the steps next to the shop, then turn left and walk fifty steps ...

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: He was like an enthusiastic tour guide, giving me all the details.

items.speaker: Kind Local
items.text: Be careful in the narrow alley and don't trip over the melons on the ground stall, or you'll be an easy target for the old man who'll try to swindle you of everything you have!

items.speaker: Kind Local
items.text: When you smell fried chickpeas, follow the aroma. Oh, and maybe buy some while you're there, help out her business? They're tasty!

items.speaker: Kind Local
items.text: And finally, when you see a couple of guys crouching by a courtyard wall, that's the base!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But it's nothing like that on the map.

items.speaker: Kind Local
items.text: Juhalerat changes every day, my friend. It's better to trust me than to trust your map.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: So I took a leap of faith. I trusted the guy.
Zeno Base, Juhalerat

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Truth be told, the place was pretty shabby. They were houses taken over from civilians, mostly.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: A perimeter wall, two courtyards, a few rows of converted barracks, and one "office."

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Several men squatted outside the wall, killing time and eyeing me as I walked in.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The guard on duty was dozing off in the shade, rifle on his lap.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Wake up. You're on watch.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I nudged the slacker with my boot. He gave me a stink eye in return and went right back to sleep.

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Don't start any trouble, little girl. Go play somewhere else.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I'm here for Bertolt.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hearing Bertolt's name, he squinted and stretched out a finger, pointing into the courtyard.

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Third house from the left, he's in there. Go ahead.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But before I could find Bertolt, he found me first.
A uniformed gentleman emerges from the house and catches sight of the young recruit.
The unfamiliar recruit runs up to the officer, handing over a letter. The piece of yellow paper is now dried out by the heat of Juhalerat's sun.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: You new here?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: A Zeno Air Force Reserve cadet. Hmm, good. A little falcon chick.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Think you can fly over the Hindu Kush? We've had many great pilots take on the mountains, but not all have made it back.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Be very careful. The mountain folk here have been hunting fierce beasts and birds for thousands of years, including eagles and falcons alike.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Compared to the careless, unreliable nature of this place, Bertolt seemed to be the most dependable soldier around.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: It's too bad you came at a bad time. I'm about to go on a mission, no time to take you under my wing, I'm afraid.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: No one can guarantee their own safe return from the next mission, rookie. You should prepare yourself for any outcome.
The girl's interest ignites.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: A mission? Then I've come at the right time. Sir, I'm here to fight, so take me with you!

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: You want to come along?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Why else would I be here? To kick rocks, shoot targets, and shuffle files all day?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Hah. For the menial tasks, you can leave them to the others. Just holler at the gate and you'll have more help than you know what to do with.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: If you want to come, come. By the way, tell me, little falcon, what does loyalty mean to you?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Not afraid of dying for a cause.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Right you are, but on the battlefield, "loyalty" is much more complicated than that.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: As for sacrifice ... Sacrifice is loyalty, and loyalty is sacrifice. Let's go with that. Come, little friend, I've gathered everyone. Let's go meet them.
A dozen soldiers are waiting in another part of the courtyard. Bertolt walks up to them with Lilya.
He starts a head count, only to find that one person is missing.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Where's Hassan?!

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: He said he was heading out to buy tea half an hour ago.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Did he seriously expect us to tolerate his frequent tea breaks that waste our time?
Just as the words leave his mouth, a robed man hurries over from the opposite side of the courtyard.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: I'm here, boss! Hassan's here!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The tardy soldier, Hassan, turned out to be the same guy who showed me the way to the base.

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: It was your turn to stand guard today, Comrade Hassan.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Me? Yes, it was my turn, but Abu said he'd cover for me. And isn't he doing a wonderful job standing guard over there? No need to worry, brother Aleksei!

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: When it's your turn, it's your turn! Those are the rules!

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Enough. Time is ticking. Aleksei, get the first aid kit ready. The rest of you, grab your gear. The truck will be here in five minutes.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Time had its own rhythm in Juhalerat. Waiting for five minutes there was more like waiting for fifteen.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Fifteen minutes minimum.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: And what should I do, boss?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Get acquainted with our new friend and keep her safe until the mission is over.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Scram. I don't need no babysitter.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Wow, boss, look at her! She's a fierce little thing. Ha!

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: When my sister was her age, she didn't even dare to talk to people while herding sheep up in the mountains. Hahaha!

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Show a little more respect for our comrade, Hassan.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Hey there, what's your name?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Her name is Lilya. She's from the academy, just like you.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: That's fantastic news! I actually just graduated from there. Did you apply for the base yourself?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Kind of. I beat a lot of people, so they let me come here.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Uh, I'm not sure what that means. I can't imagine what you've gone through to get here, but you must have some serious skills.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Oh, she's a "tough cookie," Aleksei, that's what they say nowadays!
The robed man seems quite friendly to Aleksei. Or perhaps he's just "friendly" to everyone.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Some say that brother Aleksei looks scary, but don't worry, he's actually a good man, haha!

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: He hands out candy and plays ball with the kids, smiles at everyone, speaks kindly, and even pays the locals a fair price with real money.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Outsiders have done too many terrible things in this place. The people resent us.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: It should not be like this, it should not be ... We were supposed to be here to help them defend their homes, to help them build their city.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: War makes good men better and bad men worse. Some of our comrades, and I'm ashamed to call them comrades, are downright criminals.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: It's always been like that, war. Always like that.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Those thugs all deserve to be shot!
After their brief spat, Aleksei turns his attention back to Lilya with a warm and attentive gaze.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: I ... may have said too much. Let's save the rest for later, young comrade, when we're on the road and can get to know each other better. I'll see you soon.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: If he had lived 500 years ago, he would've been the most devout ascetic of his time. Don't you agree, friend?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: He totally would have.
Aleksei hurries to the house while the others keep busy at camp, waiting for the borrowed truck from their allies.
The commander pulls the eager little falcon aside for a private word.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What's the plan, sir?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Lilya, let's talk about courage. It is a great virtue, and I have no doubt about your own courage.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: But there is no need for you to quench the fire with your own blood.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Speak plainly, sir.
Bertolt pauses, gathering his thoughts before speaking carefully.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I appreciate your enthusiasm to join us on this mission, but as young blood with so much potential, you and Aleksei are the true future of Zeno.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: And we must preserve those sparks.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: A wise warrior knows when to attack, just as they know when to decisively retreat.
The commander's words are tactful, but the hint of underestimation infuriates the battle-hungry youth.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What, you want me to punk out? Not way, I'm no chicken! I'm tough as nails, just like you guys!
She does not need anyone's protection. Never has, never will.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Chicken? That's not the right word, little falcon. I trust your tactical acumen and your willingness to sacrifice for the cause, but I don't want you to be the one to bear that burden.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: If things go south, take your broom and fly away as fast as you can. My people will cover you. Don't throw your life away here. You have to survive.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Your people? Sir. I'm one of you.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Alright, your comrades will cover you. But when I give the order to retreat, obey my command, Comrade Lilya.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Bertolt left me no room to argue. He was my commander, and I was his soldier.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I had to comply.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But I still felt he underestimated me.
The truck finally pulls up and the team assembles. Before they leave, Bertolt outlines the mission.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We are on our way to save a team of comrades. They have been trapped in the mountains by unfriendly, armed forces stirring up trouble.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Retrieve our people and the documents they've recovered, and eliminate all obstacles in your way. You know what must be done.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: That's all, comrades. Get on the truck and head out. Best of luck to us all.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But Bertolt lied.

items.speaker: Interrogator II
items.text: Stop. What do you mean by "Bertolt lied"?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: While our objectives were "search and rescue" and "recovery," he lied to the soldiers.
The interrogator nods and turns to signal the clerk.

items.speaker: Interrogator II
items.text: So who or what were you actually trying to save? Important arcanists, or something else?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Documents lost during war.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Anyway, that's what Bertolt told to me after; they were his real objective.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And those unlucky comrades were just regrettable, necessary losses.
TO BE CONTINUED…
